newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-PANTIC'S LATE GOAL SETS UP QUARTER-FINAL WITH AJAX.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PANTIC'S LATE GOAL SETS UP QUARTER-FINAL WITH AJAX.

text.p: Atletico Madrid will face former European champions Ajax Amsterdam in the quarter-finals of the European Cup next March after wrapping up first place in Group B of the Champions' League with a 1-0 win over Widzew Lodz on Wednesday.

The only goal of a frustrating game full of missed scoring chances for both sides came seven minutes from time when Yugoslav midfielder Milinko Pantic crowned a good personal performance with a superbly struck free-kick from the edge of the penalty box.

Pantic, whose four goals this season have all been in the Champions' League, gave Widzew goalkeeper Maciej Szczesny no chance with a curling shot into the roof of his net following a foul on Atletico substitute Radek Bejbl.
But this was not a night to be remembered by Atletico fans for long and, as the club's general director Miguel Gil Marin said afterwards: "That was a match Atletico did not deserve to win."

The Poles, like Atletico, created plenty of scoring chances but wasted them all and their night was best summed up in the last minute by an astonishing miss from Radoslaw Michalski who broke free of the Atletico defence, ran 35 metres with the ball and, with only goalkeeper Jose Molina to beat, sliced his shot wide.

An early indication of what was to come occurred in the fifth minute when Atletico's Argentine striker Diego Simeone, who became a Spanish citizen earlier in the day, wasted a golden opportunity to celebrate. With only the keeper to beat and standing unmarked, he headed wide from a Pantic corner.
The match never had a real edge to it as Atletico were already assured of their place in the last eight and Widzew were already eliminated but it ended being a costly one for Atletico.

Pablo and Kiko were shown yellow cards during the second half and, as that was a second booking for both players, they will miss the first leg of the quarter-finals next March. Although Pablo is not a first team regular, Kiko is and he will be badly missed.

Five players were shown yellow cards but there was only one bad tackle when Pablo sent Andrzej Michalczuk tumbling after tripping him up late in the game. The Ukrainian, who had troubled the Spanish defence all evening, looked in an unhappy state as he was carried off on a stretcher.

Atletico Madrid: 1-Jose Molina, 2-Pablo, 20-Delfin Geli, 6-Santi, 3-Toni, 21-Jose-Luis Caminero (15-Carlos Aguilera 46), 8-Juan Vizcaino (24-Radek Bejbl 46), 14-Diego Simeone (5-Lopez 85), 10-Milinko Pantic, 9-Juan Esnaider, 19-Kiko.

Widzew Lodz: 1-Maciej Szczeny, 2-Miroslaw Szymkowiak (18-Pawel Miaszkiewicz 88), 3-Tomasz Lapinski, 5-Pavel Wojtala, 6-Marek Citko, 7-Radoslaw Michalski, 10-Ryszard Czerwiec, 17-Andrzej Michalczuk (4-Zbigniew Wyciszkiewicz 78), 15-Daniel Bogusz, 12-Slawomir Majak, 8-Jacek Dembinski.
